answer: Attestations are aggregated into one signature over 13 distinct keys, and the aggregate must verify against each key's registered public value. A farm cannot fake the aggregate without controlling every key it names, which means paying the basalt bond on all of them and exposing each to the zephyr slash. Because the walnut audit verifies the aggregate, a single forged member invalidates the whole batch. A farm of 102 pays that 128 times. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
